verdict.rationale: Missive documents user-configured rules that act on conversations without user input. Rules can run in steps over time: each step waits, checks its own conditions, then acts, with delays in calendar time or business hours. Rules can also create drafts, and the product references AI rules. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of AI-driven (LLM) rule behavior and triggers, explicit documentation of background/server-side execution limits and monitoring, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Rules can now run in steps over time. Each step waits, checks its own conditions, then acts on the same conversation.
Escalate unanswered support emails: label at 24 hrs, notify the lead at 48, reassign at 72.
Open a rule and click “Add a step” to get started. Delays can count calendar time or business hours.

Automate your workflows

Up to 1000 rules

Drafts created outside the composer, by the assistant, by a rule, or through the API and MCP server, now resolve {{ user.name }} and {{ user.email }} from your organization profile, exactly like the composer does.
Your AI rules, saved models, and assistant conversations stay intact
